pages.x: Mithridates VI became king of Pontus, on the Black Sea coast of Anatolia, as a boy, after his father was poisoned. Afraid of being poisoned himself, he took small doses every day to make himself immune. He grew into a giant of a man who could speak, it was said, all 22 languages of his lands.

In 88 BC, while Rome was at war with its own allies in Italy, Mithridates swept through the Roman province of Asia, welcomed by many cities sick of Roman tax collectors. Then he ordered every Roman and Italian in the province killed on a single day.
pages.of: Romans and Italians killed in a day

pages.x: Athens joined Mithridates. Rome sent Sulla, who besieged the city, cutting down the groves of Plato's Academy for timber, and stormed it in 86 BC. He then crushed much larger armies at Chaeronea and Orchomenus, and made a quick peace so that he could hurry home to fight a civil war.

In 74 BC the king of Bithynia died and left his kingdom to Rome, and Mithridates went to war a third time. The Roman general Lucullus starved his army outside Cyzicus, invaded Pontus, and in 69 BC routed the huge army of Mithridates' son-in-law, Tigranes of Armenia, at his new capital, Tigranocerta. Then his weary troops mutinied.

Lucullus grew enormously rich in the East, and his feasts were so lavish that a Lucullan banquet still means a splendid one. The Roman writer Pliny says that he brought the first cherry trees to Italy, from Pontus.

In 66 BC Rome gave the command to Pompey, fresh from sweeping the pirates from the sea. He caught Mithridates by night and destroyed his army, and Tigranes laid his crown at Pompey's feet. Mithridates escaped around the Black Sea to the Crimea, planning, it was said, to march on Italy over the Alps.

In 63 BC his son Pharnaces led a revolt against him. Cornered at Panticapaeum, the old king took poison, but, the story goes, his body was so used to it that it would not work, and he had a soldier of his guard kill him with a sword.

Pompey reorganised the whole East. Pontus, Bithynia and Syria became Roman provinces, ringed by client kings, and he took Jerusalem. He came home the greatest man in Rome. Mithridates became a legend, and gave his name to the art of making oneself immune to poison.
pts: Three wars with Rome, 88 to 63 BC
Sulla, Lucullus and Pompey fought him
